stated_limitation: Both effects are visible in single sessions from a single animal using only openly available DANDI data and standard Pynapple tuning-curve tools, without any simulated or synthetic data.

justification.dataset: DANDI 000070 (Churchland macaque M1/PMd center-out maze reaching) is a canonical dataset for reach direction and velocity tuning.
justification.handling: Real remfile-streamed data with careful trial filtering and correct movement-epoch alignment, but no explicit single-unit quality criteria.
justification.analysis: Cosine model and circular resultant are appropriate, but no shuffle/null controls exist and the speed correlation is computed on binned tuning-curve means, inflating r.
justification.correctness: All headline numbers reproduce from the committed code and match the figures, with a minor .py-vs-README R^2 inconsistency and an inflated binned-mean correlation that does not flip the conclusion.
justification.figures: The direction and speed effects are clearly visible with labeled axes and units, examples honestly ranked by effect strength, marred only by a clipped histogram and cluttered polar labels.
justification.honesty: Examples are honestly labeled 'top' and all numbers reproduce, but the write-up mildly overstates weak population-level direction tuning and omits any caveat about the movement-phase speed confound or missing significance tests.
